Horner's Method

AlgebraAlgorithmsArithmetic
Game: Evaluate a polynomial in one repeated step, and get its derivative almost for free.
How to play: Edit any coefficient or the value of x and watch the table rebuild itself.

The coefficients run from the highest power of x down to the constant term.

Look for the math

One small recurrence evaluates a polynomial, divides it by a linear factor and finds a derivative — all at once.

The nested form

Write P(x) = (…(aₙx + aₙ₋₁)x + … + a₁)x + a₀. Starting from the leading coefficient, set bₖ = t·bₖ₊₁ + aₖ. The final b₀ is P(t). For the page's 2x⁴ − 3x³ + x + 7 at t = 2, the row is 2, 1, 2, 5, 17 — so P(2) = 17.

Quotient and derivative

The same row gives P(x) = (x − t)Q(x) + r, with Q's coefficients in the first entries and the remainder r last. Differentiating and setting x = t leaves P'(t) = Q(t), so a second Horner pass on the quotient gives the derivative. The logic test checks the value against direct evaluation, the division identity as a polynomial, and the derivative against the power rule on 500 random polynomials.

Try x = 0. What do the quotient and remainder tell you then?
